Ben / Monica — quick legal notes to shape our response to HealthOps. High-level: under CCPA/CPRA the common customer-facing designations are Service Provider (SP) and Third Party. "Operator" language appears in some state laws and vendor-specific DPA variants; for our purposes the important distinctions are:

- Service Provider (Redwood's typical stance): Processes personal information strictly on behalf of the customer, limited by contract from (i) selling the data, (ii) combining information across customers for use beyond service delivery, and (iii) retaining identifiable data beyond operational needs and deletion windows.
- Third Party/Reseller: If Redwood were to repurpose telemetry or model outputs for its own purposes (e.g., training models across customers or monetizing outputs), customers would need to treat us as a third party or seek express consent.
- Operator exceptions: Some customers (particularly in regulated verticals) ask for an "operator" carve-out — essentially a narrower SP model where Redwood's access is tightly scoped to a subset of systems (on-prem gateway / customer-managed keys) and limited telemetry is permitted for service continuity. This is negotiated case-by-case.

Suggested contractual language (short bullets we should propose):
- Purpose limitation: "Redwood will process Customer Personal Information only to provide the Services and as directed by Customer; Redwood will not sell or otherwise monetize Customer Personal Information."
- No combination clause: "Redwood shall not combine Customer Personal Information with personal information from other customers for any purpose unrelated to providing the Services."
- Telemetry minimization: "Telemetry shall be limited to operational metrics and error traces necessary for performance, and shall be pseudonymized/aggregated in transit and at rest; telemetry which contains personal identifiers shall be deleted within X days unless Customer directs otherwise."
- Edge-cache constraints: "Edge caching may store temporary generated outputs to improve latency; Redwood will not use cached outputs for model training or external analytics and will honor Customer-configured eviction TTLs and obfuscation controls."
- Audit/evidence: "Redwood will provide a telemetry dataflow diagram and sample deletion log on request and permit scoped audit access for compliance review as reasonably agreed."

Operational asks we should get from HealthOps so we can answer concretely:
1) Examples of requests/inputs that may include personal data (PHI-lite vs. purely operational IDs).
2) Whether HealthOps requires data residency/onshore fallback for logs/telemetry.
3) Preferred TTL for edge cache eviction and whether output hashing/prefixing is acceptable.
4) Whether HealthOps will accept the SP construct or insists on an "operator" exception with customer-managed keys.

If you want, I'll draft a one-page addendum (redline-ready) and a 2-slide summary for procurement that maps each ask to our standard controls.
